incidents.cause: The flight instructor's failure to maintain directional control during landing.
Fatigue cracking of the upper torque-link attach lugs on the left main landing gear strut, which resulted in separation of the left main landing gear during taxi.
The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed to avoid an aerodynamic stall during takeoff/initial climb.
A total loss of engine power for undetermined reasons, and the pilot’s failure to maintain proper control of the airplane, which led to a hard, bounced landing.
